decisions.evidence: R4 maker: 'paste this link and press Save ... the saved item appears ... with the page's title, site, and a short description filled in automatically'. R4 client: 'The one-step paste-and-save flow feels right'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-URL conforms to REF-BM-01; confirmed.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker showed 'a little thumbnail spot' / generic images. R4 client: 'I'd want the thumbnail and site icon to come from the actual page rather than be generic placeholders.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented favicon/preview were generic placeholders, diverging from REF-BM-02 (collect from target page); client supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (real page images). Maker frames this as a prototype limitation in R5, but the client's expression is a corrective/correct.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presented saving only. R4 client: 'I'd also like a chance to correct the automatically filled title or description, either while saving or afterward'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editing auto-collected title/description (REF-BM-03) was missing from the presented save scope; client requests it (before and after saving).

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presented no duplicate handling. R4 client: 'if I paste a link I've already saved, I don't want a duplicate. Please take me to the existing bookmark so I can update it instead.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Duplicate-to-edit guidance (REF-BM-06) missing from presented scope; client requests the reference requirement. Maker defers one round (R5) then delivers (R7) — same decision, not double-counted.

decisions.evidence: R5 maker offered A (fix later button), B (fix while saving), C (inline edit). R5 client: 'I'd combine B and A. When saving, I want the editable preview from B ... Afterward, I prefer the clear Edit button from A ... use that same edit screen later'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Offered alternatives differ in fulfilment: REF-BM-03 requires editing BOTH before and after saving; A=after-only, B=before-only, C=after-only. Client selects the conforming combination (B+A). Offered decision marked diverged=true per select rule.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker: both dup options 'refuse to create a second copy' and take user to existing bookmark; normalization rule http/https/www/trailing-slash. R7 client selects B and confirms the 'same link' rule.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivery of REF-BM-06; both A/B options fulfil the requirement equally, so the A/B pick is an orthogonal UI preference. URL-normalization is an equivalent implementation of 'same url'. Conforming.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker offered A (type+Enter chips), B (chips PLUS existing tags to reuse), C (comma line). R8 client: 'Option B fits best ... seeing and clicking existing tags will help me avoid accidentally creating slightly different versions of the same tag.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Alternatives differ in fulfilment: only B offers existing tags (REF-BM-10 autocomplete/reuse); A and C do not. Client selects the reference-conforming alternative; offered decision diverged=true per select rule.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker: tags shown as #chips but not clickable. R8 client: 'I'd expect clicking one on a saved bookmark to show me everything with that tag.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tag-filtering (REF-BM-11) absent from presented scope; client requests it. Maker acknowledges it's the next build (R9) and delivers R11.

decisions.evidence: R8 maker: 'The note is just a free text box' shown as a highlighted line. R8 client: 'I may write longer notes and use simple formatting such as links, bold text, or lists, so I'd want that formatting to display properly rather than showing the raw symbols.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented note was plain free text; client requests markdown rendering (REF-BM-23) missing from presented scope.

decisions.evidence: R9/R10 maker rendered bold/italic/links/lists, then headings, numbered lists, paragraph breaks. R10 client: 'Yes, that covers what I need ... formatting appears properly instead of as raw symbols.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Markdown-note rendering now conforms to REF-BM-23. R9 client request for headings/numbered lists is a within-item feature refinement (reference does not enumerate markdown features), orthogonal; final state conforms.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker: click #recipes narrows list; typing 'grid' narrows to CSS Grid; search across title/description/tags/note/site+link. R11 client: 'The basic finding flow feels right. Searching across the title, description, note, tags, and link is useful.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tag-click filter (REF-BM-11) and full-text search (REF-BM-12) delivered and conforming.

decisions.evidence: R11 maker search presented no case rule. R11 client: 'Searches should ignore capitalization.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Case-insensitive search (REF-BM-13) missing from presented basic search; client requests it.

decisions.evidence: R11 client: 'Typing #recipes should search specifically for that tag.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Typed #tag search syntax (REF-BM-14), distinct from tag-click filter, missing from presented scope; client requests it.

decisions.evidence: R11 client: 'I'd like AND, OR, and NOT, with parentheses for combinations—for example, rome AND (#article OR #book) ... If I quote a word such as "OR", it should be treated as ordinary text rather than an instruction.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Boolean operators/parentheses and the quoted-operator-as-literal rule (REF-BM-15) missing from presented scope; client requests them, matching the reference example verbatim.

decisions.evidence: R11 client: 'Quotation marks should find an exact phrase.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Quoted-phrase exact match (REF-BM-16) missing from presented scope; client requests it.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker demonstrated ROME (case-insensitive), #recipes, "ancient rome", rome AND (#article OR #book), NOT, "OR" literal. R12 client: 'the search now behaves the way I'd expect. All three decisions work for me.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivery of the advanced-search requirements; conforming. Client's request for a non-blocking 'hint' on malformed queries is orthogonal (not a reference item).

decisions.evidence: R13 maker offered A (tabs), B (All/To read/Finished switch), C (two sections); 'Mark as finished ... never deletes'. R13 client selects B and confirms move-not-delete and reversibility.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Read-later/unread-view/mark-read (REF-BM-17/18/19) conform; all three options fulfil 'view unread separately' equally, so the A/B/C pick and 'new items start To read' default are orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker presented long-content/large-collection only. R17 client: 'I'd also need to control the order—at least newest or oldest saved first, and title A–Z or Z–A. Please include sorting alongside the existing filters.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Sorting (REF-BM-22) missing from presented scope; client requests the reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: R18 maker: Sort dropdown with Newest/Oldest/Title A–Z/Z–A, default Newest, works with filters. R18 client: 'those four options cover what I need, and Newest saved is the right initial default.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivery of REF-BM-22; conforming.

decisions.evidence: R18 client: 'I'd like the app to remember my chosen order between visits, with a setting to make another option my personal default if I prefer it later.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Personal default-sort setting (REF-BM-32) missing from presented sort scope; client requests it.

decisions.evidence: R19 maker: preference persists across reload; Settings sets default order. R19 client: 'The simpler "remember my last choice" behavior matches what I meant ... Settings is still useful.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivery of default-sort setting (REF-BM-32); unified-vs-separate-default alternatives both fulfil the item, so the pick is orthogonal. Conforming.

decisions.evidence: R20 maker summary + 'May I start implementing this scope?'. R20 client: 'Not quite yet ... Opening a bookmark should take me to the original page.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Navigate-to-original (REF-BM-08) omitted from the proposed implementation scope; client surfaces and requests it.

decisions.evidence: R20 client: 'I also need to edit its address, not only its title and description'.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Editing the url (REF-BM-04) omitted from proposed scope; client requests it.

decisions.evidence: R20 client: '... and permanently delete it when appropriate.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Delete (REF-BM-05) omitted from proposed scope; client requests it.

decisions.evidence: R20 client: 'I need a separate Archive. Archiving should hide a bookmark from the normal collection and search without deleting it, with an Archived view where I can restore it. This is separate from whether I've finished reading it.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Archive-hide (REF-BM-26), archive-vs-delete distinction/reversibility (REF-BM-27), and archived view (REF-BM-28) omitted from proposed scope; client requests all three.

decisions.evidence: R20 client: 'I need to select several bookmarks—or everything matching the current search or filters—and add or remove tags, change read status, archive, or delete them together.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Bulk selection/actions (REF-BM-20) and bulk-over-whole-filtered-collection (REF-BM-21) omitted from proposed scope; client requests them.

decisions.evidence: R20 client: 'I'd like to save a useful combination of search text and included or excluded tags, so I can return to that same filtered view later.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Bundle/saved view (REF-BM-29) omitted from proposed scope; client requests it, matching the reference bundle definition (search term + included/excluded tags).

decisions.evidence: R20 client: 'I want a preserved copy of a page ... as well as an option to save it through the Internet Archive. For a PDF link, the preserved copy should be the PDF itself.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Local snapshot with PDF rule (REF-BM-24) and Internet Archive snapshot (REF-BM-25) omitted from proposed scope; client requests them, including the PDF edge case.

decisions.evidence: R20 client: 'I need to bring in my existing browser bookmarks and export the collection again without losing titles, tags, or saved dates.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Import (REF-BM-30) and export (REF-BM-31) with title/tag/date preservation omitted from proposed scope; client requests them.

decisions.evidence: R20 client: 'Settings should also cover how many items are shown and the text size, not just sorting.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Displayed-items and font-size settings (REF-BM-32) omitted from the proposed settings scope; client requests them (distinct timing from the R18 default-sort request).

decisions.evidence: R21 maker: click title opens original in new tab; Edit exposes an 'Address (link)' field; Delete confirms permanently. R21 client: 'Opening the original in a new tab, keeping the existing details when I edit the address, and always confirming permanent deletion all behave as I'd want.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivery of REF-BM-08/04/05; conforming. A/B action-layout pick and 'keep read-status visible' are orthogonal UI preferences.

decisions.evidence: R21 maker presented address editing without dedup on the new address. R21 client: 'If I change the address to one that is already saved, it should also prevent a duplicate and guide me to the existing bookmark.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Duplicate-prevention (REF-BM-06) not applied to the edit-address path in the presentation; client extends the reference dedup rule to that case.

decisions.evidence: R22 maker: Archive hides from All/To read/Finished and search; Archived view with Restore or permanent Delete; separate from read status. R22 client: 'The behavior is right ... archived items stay out of the normal views and searches, and I can restore them or deliberately delete them permanently.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivery of REF-BM-26/27/28; A/B navigation pick is orthogonal. Conforming.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker: 'Select all matching (N)' acts on everything the current search/filters show. R23 client: '"Select all matching" behaving within the current search, tag, and status filters is exactly right, and confirming bulk deletion is essential.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivery of bulk-over-filtered-collection (REF-BM-21); conforming. A/B selection-mode pick is orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker presented bulk Mark Finished, Add tags, Archive, Delete. R23 client: 'The action set needs two additions to be complete: I should be able to mark the selection either Finished or To read, and both add and remove tags from all selected bookmarks.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented bulk set omitted un-finish (To read) and remove-tags; REF-BM-20 requires bulk add/remove tags and read/unread. Client extends to complete the reference bulk action set.

decisions.evidence: R24 maker: saved view stores search text + included/excluded tags as a live re-running rule; asks whether status should be included. R24 client: 'A saved view should be a reusable rule that updates as the collection changes ... Keep To read/Finished status and sorting out of the saved view.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivery of REF-BM-29; the reference bundle = search term + included/excluded tags, so keeping status/sort out is reference-conforming. Conforming.

decisions.evidence: R25 maker: preserved copy survives original disappearing; PDF copy is the PDF; Internet Archive is a separate explicit action; A (automatic) vs B (on-demand). R25 client: 'Automatic copies best support the goal ... The saved copy should be self-contained ... Saving a PDF as the PDF itself is correct, and sending something to the Internet Archive should remain a separate, explicit action.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivery of REF-BM-24/25 with the PDF rule; auto-vs-on-demand timing and self-contained detail are orthogonal/equivalent to the reference requirement. Conforming. Maker's prototype-simulation caveat is an execution note, not a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: R26 maker: import maps browser folders→tags, preserves original dates, skips duplicates. R26 client: 'folders becoming tags is the right mapping, and preserving the original saved dates while skipping duplicates is exactly what I'd expect.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delivery of import (REF-BM-30) with title/tag/date preservation; conforming.

decisions.evidence: R26 maker described export only as 'a re-importable file that loses none of your titles, tags, or saved dates' (format unstated). R26 client: 'The exported file should use the standard browser-bookmark HTML format so browsers and other bookmark tools can open it ... include the whole collection, including archived bookmarks.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented export did not commit to the Netscape/standard interoperable format; client supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (REF-BM-31 Netscape HTML export).

decisions.evidence: R27 maker final scope summary + 'may I start implementing it?'. R27 client: 'the previously confirmed behavior where clicking a bookmark's title or image opens the original page in a new tab should remain part of the scope even though it isn't listed explicitly here.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. The final scope summary again omitted REF-BM-08 (open original); client re-catches the omission and re-asserts it. Distinct presentation from R20, so a new decision at different timing.
